reason: The text establishes a clear conditional relationship between improper approach to God's sacred space and death. God commands specific sanctification protocols and strict boundary enforcement, with explicit warnings that 'all who touch the mountain will surely be put to death' (כָּל־ הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בָּהָ֖ר מ֥וֹת יוּמָֽת). The text repeatedly warns of deadly consequences for not following prescribed behaviors—priests must sanctify themselves 'lest Yahweh break out against them,' and people are forbidden from approaching the mountain 'lest many fall.' These detailed instructions on sanctification, preparation, and boundary-respecting constitute the proper protocol for worshiping/approaching God, and failure to observe them results in death.
